movers.name: Immanuel Kant
movers.description: Immanuel Kant was a German philosopher. Born in Königsberg in the Kingdom of Prussia, he is considered one of the central thinkers of the Enlightenment.

movers.name: Aristotle
movers.description: Aristotle was an ancient Greek philosopher and polymath.

movers.name: René Descartes
movers.description: René Descartes was a French philosopher, mathematician, and scientist whose work was foundational to mathematics and modern philosophy.

movers.name: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz
movers.description: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz was a German polymath active as a mathematician, philosopher, scientist, and diplomat who is credited, alongside Isaac Newton, with the creation of calculus in addition to many other branches of mathematics, such as binary arithmetic and statistics.

movers.name: Karl Marx
movers.description: Karl Marx was a German philosopher, social and political theorist, and revolutionary socialist.

movers.name: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel
movers.description: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel was a German philosopher and a major figure in the tradition of German idealism.

movers.name: Plato
movers.description: Plato was an ancient Greek philosopher of Classical Athens who is most commonly considered the foundational thinker of the Western philosophical tradition.

movers.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
movers.description: Friedrich Wilhelm Nietzsche was a German philosopher and writer who started his career as a classical philologist and turned to philosophy early in his academic career.

movers.name: Edmund Husserl
movers.description: Edmund Gustav Albrecht Husserl was an Austrian and German philosopher and mathematician who established the school of phenomenology.

movers.name: Baruch Spinoza
movers.description: Baruch Spinoza, also known under his Latinized pen name Benedictus de Spinoza, was a philosopher of Portuguese-Jewish origin who was born and lived in the Dutch Republic.

movers.name: Jesus
movers.description: Jesus, also known as Jesus Christ, Jesus of Nazareth, and by various other names and titles, was a 1st-century Jewish preacher and religious leader in the Roman province of Judaea.

movers.name: Arthur Schopenhauer
movers.description: Arthur Schopenhauer, also known as the “Philosopher of Pessimism”, was a German philosopher and writer.

movers.name: Plotinus
movers.description: Plotinus was an ancient Greek philosopher, born and raised in Roman Egypt.

movers.name: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
movers.description: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe was a German polymath who is widely regarded as the most influential writer in the German language.

movers.name: Thomas Hobbes
movers.description: Thomas Hobbes was an English philosopher and political theorist, best known for his 1651 book Leviathan, in which he expounds an influential formulation of social contract theory.

movers.name: Galileo Galilei
movers.description: Galileo di Vincenzo Bonaiuti de' Galilei, commonly referred to as Galileo Galilei or mononymously as Galileo, was an Italian astronomer, physicist, engineer and polymath.

movers.name: Thomas Aquinas
movers.description: Thomas Aquinas was an Italian Dominican friar and priest, theologian, and philosopher.

movers.name: Dante Alighieri
movers.description: Dante Alighieri, widely known mononymously as Dante, was an Italian poet, writer, and philosopher.

movers.name: Erasmus
movers.description: Desiderius Erasmus Roterodamus, commonly known in English as Erasmus of Rotterdam or simply Erasmus, was a Dutch humanist, theologian, and philosopher.

movers.name: Kitarō Nishida
movers.description: Kitarō Nishida was a Japanese moral philosopher, philosopher of mathematics and science, and religious scholar.

movers.name: Bertrand Russell
movers.description: Bertrand Arthur William Russell, 3rd Earl Russell, was an English philosopher, logician, and social reformer.

movers.name: Roger Bacon
movers.description: Roger Bacon, also known by the scholastic accolade Doctor Mirabilis, was a medieval English polymath, philosopher, scientist, theologian and Franciscan friar who placed considerable emphasis on the study of nature through empiricism.

movers.name: Thomas Carlyle
movers.description: Thomas Carlyle was a Scottish essayist, historian and philosopher.

movers.name: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling
movers.description: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling was a German philosopher.

movers.name: Francis Bacon
movers.description: Francis Bacon, 1st Viscount St Alban was an English philosopher and statesman who served as Attorney General and Lord Chancellor of England under King James I.

movers.name: Origen
movers.description: Origen of Alexandria, also known as Origen Adamantius, was an early Christian theologian and ascetic.

movers.name: Martin Heidegger
movers.description: Martin Heidegger was a German philosopher whose work was central to the development of phenomenology, hermeneutics, and existentialism.

movers.name: John Locke
movers.description: John Locke was an English philosopher and physician, widely regarded as one of the most influential of the Enlightenment thinkers and commonly known as the "father of liberalism".

movers.name: Augustine of Hippo
movers.description: Augustine of Hippo, also well-known as Saint Augustine, was a Christian theologian and philosopher from Thagaste, Numidia Cirtensis and the Bishop of Hippo Regius.

movers.name: Cicero
movers.description: Marcus Tullius Cicero was a Roman statesman, lawyer, scholar, philosopher, orator, and writer who tried to uphold optimate principles during the political crises of the Roman Republic that led to the establishment of the Roman Empire.

movers.name: David Hume
movers.description: David Hume was a Scottish philosopher, historian, economist and essayist who is known for his highly influential system of empiricism, philosophical scepticism and metaphysical naturalism.

movers.name: Friedrich Hayek
movers.description: Friedrich August von Hayek was an Austrian economist and philosopher.

movers.name: Nicolaus Copernicus
movers.description: Nicolaus Copernicus was a Renaissance polymath who formulated a model of the universe that placed the Sun rather than Earth at its center.

movers.name: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
movers.description: Samuel Taylor Coleridge was an English poet, literary critic, philosopher, and theologian who was a founder of the Romantic Movement in England and a member of the Lake Poets with his friend William Wordsworth.

movers.name: Diogenes Laertius
movers.description: Diogenes Laërtius was a biographer of the Greek philosophers.

movers.name: Heraclitus
movers.description: Heraclitus was a pre-Socratic Greek philosopher from the city of Ephesus, which was then part of the Persian Empire.

movers.name: Sigmund Freud
movers.description: Sigmund Freud was an Austrian neurologist and the founder of psychoanalysis, a clinical method for evaluating and treating pathologies arising from conflicts in the psyche through dialogue between patient and psychoanalyst, and the distinctive theory of mind and human agency derived from it.

movers.name: Henri Bergson
movers.description: Henri-Louis Bergson was a French philosopher who was influential in the traditions of analytic philosophy and continental philosophy, especially during the first half of the 20th century until the Second World War, but also after 1966 when Gilles Deleuze published Le Bergsonisme.

movers.name: Jean Bodin
movers.description: Jean Bodin was a French jurist and political philosopher, member of the Parlement of Paris and professor of law at the University of Toulouse.

movers.name: William James
movers.description: William James was an American philosopher and psychologist.
